title: Microsoft Teams: third-party synthetic audio and video detection in meetings
summary: The briefing passes: the policy commands, provider permissions, opt-in deployment and revised rollout window are supported. Minor gaps remain between the governance checklist and the controls table for permission grants, policy assignment and event review.

claims.claim: Teams plans to surface certified third-party synthetic audio and video detection signals in meetings.
claims.quote: Third-party detection solutions analyze meeting media for signs of synthetic or manipulated audio and video and send detection signals to Teams, enabling integrated in-meeting experiences and controls.

claims.claim: Synthetic media detection is performed by the third-party provider.
claims.quote: Important: Synthetic media detection is performed by the third-party provider.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Teams supplies the platform integration and experiences for surfacing and acting on supported providers' detection signals.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams provides the platform integration and experiences for surfacing and acting on detection signals from supported providers.

claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Targeted Release"]

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Scope: Prerequisites; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft asks administrators using this capability to select a provider, deploy its app through Manage apps, grant permissions and configure meeting policies.
claims.quote: administrators should evaluate and select a supported detection provider, deploy the provider app through Manage apps in the Teams admin center, grant required permissions, and configure applicable Teams meeting policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The notice says providers may analyse meeting audio/video and asks administrators to review provider terms, data handling and compliance before enabling.
claims.quote: Certified third-party providers may analyze meeting audio/video signals for synthetic media detection. Review provider terms, data handling, and compliance documentation before enabling.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Third-party detection requires administrator configuration of a provider rather than starting automatically in existing meetings.
claims.quote: The default value, the zero GUID (00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000), selects no provider when Microsoft Detection is unavailable, or Microsoft Detection when it is available. It does not select a third-party provider.

claims.claim: The Graph beta reportSyntheticMedia action is intended for certified third-party detection bots admitted to the call to flag a participant.
claims.quote: This action is intended for certified third-party audio and video synthetic media detection bots admitted to the meeting call. The detection bot calls this action to flag a participant whose stream it identifies as AI-generated or synthetic media.

claims.claim: Detection results propagate to all participants through roster updates.
claims.quote: The detection result is propagated to all participants via roster updates.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Prerequisites; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A third-party bot can report detections only after the meeting tenant administrator grants Calls.ReportSyntheticMedia.All application permission.
claims.quote: Third-party bots can invoke this action only when the meeting tenant administrator grants the app the `Calls.ReportSyntheticMedia.All` application permission.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: SyntheticMediaDetection and SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId configure a meeting policy to use a supported provider's Teams App ID.
claims.quote: Specifies the Teams App ID (GUID) of the detection provider to use for synthetic audio/video analysis. For third-party detection, use only the Teams App ID of a supported certified detection provider and set SyntheticMediaDetection to Enabled.

claims.quote:
| App name | Reality Defender RealMeeting |
| ID | WA200012072 |
| Office 365 clients supported | Microsoft Teams |

claims.quote:

claims.claim: Learn has no overview page describing this feature's participant experience at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "synthetic" "detection" "Teams" "overview"; Teams synthetic media detection participant flagged response controls rescan remove participant overview. Opened reportSyntheticMedia, provider listings, meeting-policies-overview and SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents; no feature overview found.

claims.claim: Reality Defender's listing declares Calls.AccessMedia.All application permission for real-time meeting audio and video access.
claims.quote: Calls.AccessMedia.All | application | The app is a meeting-recording bot, so it needs Graph to join Teams meetings and access the real-time audio and video media in order to run authenticity and deepfake analysis.

claims.claim: Reality Defender's listing is developer self-assessment information whose accuracy Microsoft does not guarantee.
claims.quote: The information on this page is based on a self-assessment report provided by the app developer on the security, compliance, and data handling practices followed by this app. Microsoft makes no guarantees regarding the accuracy of the information.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents is an advanced hunting table for synthetic media detection events in Teams.
claims.quote: The `SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents` table in the advanced hunting schema contains details about synthetic media (deepfake) detection events in Microsoft Teams in your organization.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The hunting table is populated from Defender for Office 365 and requires that service to be deployed for queries to work.
claims.quote: This advanced hunting table is populated by records from Microsoft Defender for Office 365. If your organization hasn't deployed the service in Microsoft Defender, queries that use the table don't work or return any results.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The table has data only with an approved detection engine, including GetReal, Pindrop, Reality Defender and Resemble AI.
claims.quote: This table contains data only if you're using an approved detection engine: Microsoft or a third-party engine (GetReal, Pindrop, Reality Defender, or Resemble AI).

claims.claim: The table can identify detected users by display name.
claims.quote: | `DetectedUserDisplayName` | `string` | Display name of the user flagged as using synthetic media |

claims.claim: The table contains meeting identifiers, names or URLs.
claims.quote:
| `SourceContextUrl` | `string` | URL of the source (for example, the meeting URL or file URL) |
| `SourceContextName` | `string` | Name of the source (for example, the meeting, file, or email name) |

claims.claim: Successfully saving the policy does not confirm the provider App ID is supported or that its bot can join.
claims.quote: Successfully saving the policy does not guarantee that the App ID identifies a supported provider or that the detection bot can join meetings.

claims.claim: An incorrect or unsupported provider App ID can prevent the detection bot from joining eligible meetings.
claims.quote: An incorrect or unsupported App ID can prevent the detection bot from joining eligible meetings.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented a provider-independent Teams response workflow for synthetic media detections.
claims.quote: Searched: "synthetic media" "Teams" "response"; "synthetic" "Teams" "rescan" "controls". Opened reportSyntheticMedia, Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy, SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents and both provider listings; found reporting and provider-specific actions, not a common response workflow.

claims.claim: Reality Defender's publisher-attested listing says hosts can rescan a participant.
claims.quote: Hosts can rescan a participant or end the meeting if manipulation is detected.

claims.claim: Reality Defender's publisher-attested listing says hosts can end the meeting if manipulation is detected.
claims.quote: Hosts can rescan a participant or end the meeting if manipulation is detected.

claims.claim: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy at a time.
claims.quote: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy and one events policy at a time.

claims.claim: Users receive the global meeting policy unless a custom policy is created and assigned.
claims.quote: Users get the global policy unless you create and assign a custom policy.

claims.quote: Searched: Teams third-party synthetic media detection licensing price meter Teams Premium providers; "third-party" "synthetic" "Teams" license pricing. Opened Teams Premium licensing, Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy, reportSyntheticMedia and both provider listings; no integration price found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Microsoft sources checked do not state the certified providers' fees.
claims.quote: Searched: "third-party" "synthetic" "Teams" license pricing. Opened Reality Defender RealMeeting and Pindrop Pulse listings; read purchase-third-party-apps search excerpts and Teams Premium licensing. No named detection-provider fee found; roadmap and MC1509787 give none.

claims.claim: Hunting synthetic media detections is a Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 capability.
claims.quote:
Microsoft 365 E5 and Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 extend Teams protection with a set of extra capabilities designed to disrupt the attack chain:
[...]
Hunting on synthetic media (deepfake) detections in Teams

claims.claim: No Teams admin center setting for SyntheticMediaDetection and SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams SyntheticMediaDetection SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId Teams admin center setting third party detection; "SyntheticMediaDetection" "admin center". Opened Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy and meeting-policies-overview; results document PowerShell, not a feature-specific UI.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Scope: Users and policies; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy-name> -SyntheticMediaDetection Enabled -SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId <supported-provider-app-id> permits configured-provider detection for meetings organised by assigned users.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "SyntheticDetectionPolicy" -SyntheticMediaDetection Enabled -SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId "<supported-provider-app-id>"
[...]
for meetings organized by users assigned this policy, when the feature and provider are available.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps is the page for allowing or blocking the provider app.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps.
2. Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked <value> is a documented MicrosoftTeams PowerShell call for changing tenant app state.
claims.quote:
PS C:\> Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true
[...]
-Id: Application ID of Microsoft Teams app.
[...]
-IsBlocked: The state of the app in the tenant.

claims.claim: The Update-M365TeamsApp reference describes its -IsBlocked $true example as unblocking.
claims.quote:
PS C:\> Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true

Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Administrators can block an app by selecting it in Teams apps > Manage apps and choosing Block.
claims.quote: Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: Some apps are Blocked by publisher until an administrator follows publisher configuration guidance.
claims.quote: Before an admin allows an agent or app, it shows as Blocked by publisher in the admin center. Before you allow it for users, follow the publisher's guidance to configure it.

claims.claim: Setting SyntheticMediaDetection to Disabled disables detection for meetings organised by assigned users regardless of the configured provider.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "SyntheticDetectionPolicy" -SyntheticMediaDetection Disabled
[...]
disables synthetic audio/video detection for meetings organized by users assigned this policy, regardless of the configured detection provider.

claims.claim: Disabling SyntheticMediaDetection leaves SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId unchanged.
claims.quote: The SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId value is unchanged.

claims.claim: SyntheticMediaDetection defaults to Enabled, permitting detection when a configured provider is available.
claims.quote: Enabled: Permits synthetic media detection when a configured detection provider is available. This is the default value. To configure a third-party provider, also set the SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId parameter.

claims.claim: SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId defaults to the zero GUID, which does not select a third-party provider.
claims.quote: The default value, the zero GUID (00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000), selects no provider when Microsoft Detection is unavailable, or Microsoft Detection when it is available. It does not select a third-party provider.

claims.claim: The App ID reference refers to Microsoft Detection when it is available.
claims.quote: selects no provider when Microsoft Detection is unavailable, or Microsoft Detection when it is available.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference does not state the administrator role required to run it.
claims.quote: Searched: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy Update-M365TeamsApp required admin role SyntheticMediaDetection. Opened Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy and searched its full fetched text for role and administrator; no required role is specified on that reference page.

claims.claim: The Update-M365TeamsApp reference does not state the administrator role required to run it.
claims.quote: Searched: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy Update-M365TeamsApp required admin role SyntheticMediaDetection. Opened and read the complete Update-M365TeamsApp reference; it describes administrators generally but specifies no required role.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout, permission-grant bullet
claims.claim: The checklist instructs readers to grant application permissions without a corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: "Grant only the permissions the provider needs, including Calls.ReportSyntheticMedia.All if the provider requests it." versus "Granting application permissions such as Calls.ReportSyntheticMedia.All ... have no rows in the table".
claims.fix: Remove the At rollout bullet 'Grant only the permissions the provider needs, including `Calls.ReportSyntheticMedia.All` if the provider requests it.' The table has no permission-grant control row; retain the documented prerequisite in Scope.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout, pilot-policy bullet
claims.claim: The checklist instructs readers to assign the pilot meeting policy without a corresponding controls-table row for assignment.
claims.quote: "Set SyntheticMediaDetection and SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId on a pilot meeting policy ... and assign it to pilot users." versus "assigning the pilot meeting policy ... have no rows in the table".
claims.fix: Remove ', and assign it to pilot users' from the At rollout policy-setting bullet. The existing row documents updating a policy, not assigning one.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout, detection-event review bullet
claims.claim: The checklist instructs readers to review detection events without a corresponding monitoring row in the controls table.
claims.quote: "Review SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents in Defender advanced hunting if Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 is licensed and deployed and an approved detection engine is in use." versus "reviewing detection events have no rows in the table".
claims.fix: Remove the After rollout bullet 'Review `SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents` in Defender advanced hunting if Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 is licensed and deployed and an approved detection engine is in use.' The table does not document event review.
